## Goal

Notebooks 03 to 07 found, one at a time, several points that stop us from rebuilding the case study 2 network from
public data. Here we gather them in one place. For each limit, we **call the functions of the pipeline** (or reload
the saved outputs of the earlier notebooks) and **show what comes out**, so that each statement can be checked.

The limits are ordered along the pipeline: data → software → gene selection → input table → MIIC run → network.

This notebook only covers case study 2. Some limits of case study 1 (origin and version of the NicheNet pairs,
ribosomal genes kept by the tutorial, pooling of steady-state and infected cells) do not apply here.

**Inputs:** the authors' files in `data/case2/causalccc_server_w0788tM1wzXGHLzNaKKa/`, CellChat's dataset in
`data/case2/cellchat/`, and the saved results of notebooks 04, 05 and 07 (`results/case2/`). Nothing is recomputed
except small checks: the notebook runs in about a minute.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(Seurat)
library(miic)

root <- getwd()
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))) {
  if (dirname(root) == root) stop("Repository root not found. Open the repository folder in Positron.")
  root <- dirname(root)
}
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))

job_dir  <- file.path(root, "data", "case2", "causalccc_server_w0788tM1wzXGHLzNaKKa")
cellchat <- file.path(root, "data", "case2", "cellchat", "data_humanSkin_CellChat.rda")
nb04_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "04_rerun_miic")
nb05_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "05_rebuild_input")
nb07_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "07_differences")

cell_types <- c("Fibroblasts", "T_cell", "DCs")
strip      <- function(v) str_remove_all(v, "_(Fibroblasts|T_cell|DCs)")

mosaic      <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "input.tsv"), guess_max = Inf, show_col_types = FALSE)
state_order <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "clean_state_order.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
lr_pairs    <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "clean_interact_edges.tsv"),
                        col_names = c("ligand", "receptor"), show_col_types = FALSE)
lr_links    <- link_name(lr_pairs$ligand, lr_pairs$receptor)

# Cell type of each row (which cell type has values) and of each column (which cell type it belongs to)
row_type <- case_when(!is.na(mosaic$labels_Fibroblasts) ~ "Fibroblasts",
                      !is.na(mosaic$labels_T_cell)      ~ "T_cell",
                      !is.na(mosaic$labels_DCs)         ~ "DCs")
col_type <- column_cell_type(mosaic, row_type)

rebuilt   <- readRDS(file.path(nb05_dir, "rebuild_inputs.rds"))
mi_tables <- readRDS(file.path(nb05_dir, "mi_tables.rds"))
lr_roles  <- rebuilt$lr_roles

# Short helper: run an expression and report whether it fails, and with which message
try_call <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch({ invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(force(expr)))); "no error" },
           error = \(e) paste("ERROR:", conditionMessage(e)))
}
```

# Part 1 – Data and software

## 1. The raw counts are not provided

CausalCCC needs **raw counts**. The only public version of the 7,563 cells is the CellChat example dataset
`data_humanSkin`, which contains normalised values.

```{r}
#| label: raw-counts

load(cellchat)   # creates data_humanSkin
norm <- data_humanSkin$data

# Largest distance to a whole number: raw counts would give 0
tibble(object = "CellChat matrix (data_humanSkin$data)",
       example_values = paste(round(head(norm@x, 5), 3), collapse = ", "),
       largest_distance_to_a_whole_number = max(abs(norm@x - round(norm@x))))
```

The values are not counts. We can recover the counts only by undoing the normalisation, by a reasoning that is
not documented anywhere (smallest value of each cell = count of 1; notebook 05):

```{r}
#| label: recovered-counts

cell_of_value <- rep(seq_len(ncol(norm)), diff(norm@p))
library_size  <- as.numeric(10000 / expm1(tapply(norm@x, cell_of_value, min)))
recovered     <- expm1(norm@x) * library_size[cell_of_value] / 10000

tibble(largest_distance_to_a_whole_number = max(abs(recovered - round(recovered))),
       identical_to_notebook_05_counts    = all(round(recovered) == rebuilt$counts@x))
```

The recovery is exact, but this input data and its normalisation are not described in the tutorial or the paper.
Moreover, nothing tells us how the authors' cells were selected, or which preprocessing produced the CellChat
dataset itself (see section 11).

## 2. The wrapper does not run on a current installation

We build a small Seurat object (200 cells) from the recovered counts and call the CausalCCC functions on it.

```{r}
#| label: seurat-object

set.seed(1)
meta <- rebuilt$meta
keep <- c(sample(which(meta$cell_type == "DCs"), 100), sample(which(meta$cell_type == "Fibroblasts"), 100))
so   <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = rebuilt$counts[, keep], meta.data = meta[keep, ])
so
packageVersion("SeuratObject")
```

**The gene-selection function fails with Seurat 5.** `causalCCC.MIselection()` reads the counts with
`GetAssayData(..., slot = "counts")`, an argument that no longer exists.

```{r}
#| label: slot-error

try_call(causalCCC.MIselection(so, interact_ident = "cell_type", oneinteract = "DCs",
                               goi = c("CXCR4", "CCR7"), metadata_list = c("labels", "condition")))
```

**The data-frame input does not work either.** The wrapper looks for the ligands and receptors among
`row.names(data_input)`, which are cell names:

```{r}
#| label: data-frame-input

df <- cbind(meta[keep, ], as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(rebuilt$counts[c("CXCR4", "CCR7"), keep]))))
head(row.names(df), 3)
c("CXCR4", "CCR7") %in% row.names(df)
```

**One sender and one receiver only.** The wrapper takes a single `senders_name` and a single `receivers_name`, whereas
case study 2 has three cell types that are both sender and receiver:

```{r}
#| label: wrapper-arguments

intersect(names(formals(causalCCC.wrapper)), c("senders_name", "receivers_name", "n_genes_senders", "n_genes_receivers",
                                               "goi_senders", "goi_receivers", "metadata_senders", "metadata_receivers"))
```

**The suffixes do not match the authors' table.** The mosaic function writes `_senders` and `_receivers`; the authors'
table uses the cell-type names:

```{r}
#| label: suffixes

body_lines <- deparse(causalCCC.mosaic)
trimws(body_lines[str_detect(body_lines, "senders|receivers") & str_detect(body_lines, "paste|_")]) |> head(6)

tibble(variables_with_suffix_senders_or_receivers = sum(str_detect(names(mosaic), "_senders|_receivers")),
       variables_with_a_cell_type_suffix          = sum(str_detect(names(mosaic), "_(Fibroblasts|T_cell|DCs)$")))
```

The authors therefore did not obtain their table with a single call of the published wrapper, and we do not have the
parameters they used.

# Part 2 – Gene selection

## 3. The selection settings are not documented

`causalCCC.MIselection()` has settings (number of genes, features of interest, metadata) whose values are not in the
paper or in the tutorial. We run the selection with the published defaults and with the settings found in notebook 07,
using the saved MI tables, and compare with the authors' genes.

```{r}
#| label: selection-functions

authors_selected <- map(set_names(cell_types), \(t) {
  genes <- unique(strip(names(mosaic)[col_type == t & !str_detect(names(mosaic), "^(labels|condition)_")]))
  setdiff(genes, lr_roles$gene[lr_roles$cell_type == t])
})

directions <- lr_pairs |>
  transmute(sender = col_type[ligand], receiver = col_type[receptor],
            ligand = strip(ligand), receptor = strip(receptor))

mi_by_type <- split(mi_tables, mi_tables$cell_type)

# One wrapper run per sender -> receiver direction, genes pooled per cell type (protocol B of notebook 05)
run_protocol <- function(meta_sender, meta_receiver, cap = 8, n_genes = default_n_genes) {
  one_side <- function(t, goi, meta) {
    goi <- head(unique(goi), cap)
    select_genes(mi_by_type[[t]], foi = c(goi, meta), n_genes = n_genes(goi))
  }
  runs <- directions |>
    group_by(sender, receiver) |>
    summarise(sender_genes   = list(one_side(first(sender), ligand, meta_sender)),
              receiver_genes = list(one_side(first(receiver), receptor, meta_receiver)),
              .groups = "drop")
  map(set_names(cell_types), \(t) {
    unique(c(unlist(runs$sender_genes[runs$sender == t]), unlist(runs$receiver_genes[runs$receiver == t])))
  })
}

score <- function(selected, protocol) {
  map(cell_types, \(t) {
    ours <- setdiff(selected[[t]], c(lr_roles$gene[lr_roles$cell_type == t], "labels", "condition"))
    tibble(protocol, cell_type = t,
           authors_genes = length(authors_selected[[t]]),
           missing = length(setdiff(authors_selected[[t]], ours)),
           extra   = length(setdiff(ours, authors_selected[[t]])))
  }) |> list_rbind()
}

both_metadata <- c("labels", "condition")
```

```{r}
#| label: selection-comparison

protocols <- list(
  "Published defaults: cap of 8, default n_genes, both metadata" = run_protocol(both_metadata, both_metadata, 8, default_n_genes),
  "Same with 25 genes per run"                                   = run_protocol(both_metadata, both_metadata, 8, \(goi) 25),
  "No cap, 25 genes, `labels` only"                              = run_protocol("labels", "labels", Inf, \(goi) 25),
  "No cap, 25 genes, both metadata (found in notebook 07)"       = run_protocol(both_metadata, both_metadata, Inf, \(goi) 25))

imap(protocols, \(selected, name) score(selected, name)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(protocol = factor(protocol, levels = names(protocols))) |>
  group_by(protocol) |>
  summarise(authors_genes = sum(authors_genes), missing = sum(missing), extra = sum(extra))
```

Only the last combination (both metadata, no cap, 25 genes) reproduces the authors' selection exactly (0 missing, 0 extra). None of its settings (25
genes, no cap of 8, both metadata as features of interest) is stated in the paper, and the first two differ from the
default of the published wrapper. Dropping `condition` already loses 4 genes.

**The cap of 8.** The wrapper only uses the first 8 ligands or receptors of a run as features of interest. The order
of the L-R pairs therefore decides which genes are selected. For example, TMEM219 and TNFRSF14 are beyond the cap in
two directions:

```{r}
#| label: receptor-order

directions |>
  filter(receiver == "DCs") |>
  group_by(sender) |>
  summarise(receptors = paste(seq_along(unique(receptor)), unique(receptor), sep = ".", collapse = " "))
```

# Part 3 – The input table

## 4. The input contains duplicated columns

The authors' `input.tsv` has 14 genes that appear **twice in the same cell type, as two identical columns**. The
duplication is in the table `input.tsv` itself (two columns), and so also in `clean_state_order.tsv` (two rows, one per
column).

```{r}
#| label: duplicated-columns

dup <- duplicated_columns(mosaic, row_type, col_type)

duplicates <- tibble(cell_type = col_type[dup], column_2 = dup) |>
  mutate(column_1 = map2_chr(column_2, cell_type, \(d, t) {
    block <- mosaic[row_type == t, col_type == t]
    names(block)[match(TRUE, map_lgl(as.list(block), \(column) identical(column, block[[d]])))]
  }),
  identical_values = map2_lgl(column_1, column_2, \(a, b) identical(mosaic[[a]], mosaic[[b]]))) |>
  select(cell_type, column_1, column_2, identical_values)

nrow(duplicates)
duplicates
```

The two copies of a gene have different names (one carries an extra cell-type suffix) and are two separate variables
for MIIC, as shown by the state-order file:

```{r}
#| label: duplicates-state-order

state_order |>
  filter(var_names %in% unlist(duplicates[1, c("column_1", "column_2")])) |>
  select(var_names, var_type, group)
```

**A likely origin** is the pooling of the six wrapper runs (one per direction): the same gene can be selected on the
sender side in some runs and on the receiver side in others, and get two names. The naming rule tested in notebook 05
predicts 11 of the 14 duplicates, but also 24 that the authors' table does not have, so the exact origin remains
unknown. The pooling script is not available.

## 5. The strongest link of the network is an artefact

Identical columns are linked as strongly as possible. In the authors' network, the strongest gene–gene link is between
two copies of the same gene, and the L-R links take its strength:

```{r}
#| label: strongest-link

edges_authors <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "edgesList.miic.summary.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE)

edges_authors |>
  filter(type == "P", !link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links) |>
  arrange(desc(info_shifted)) |>
  select(x, y, info_shifted, infOrt) |>
  head(3)

edges_authors |>
  filter(link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links) |>
  summarise(L_R_links = n(), strength = unique(info_shifted))
```

# Part 4 – The MIIC run

## 6. The run settings are not those of `miic()`, and they are not in the paper

The settings used by the server are only visible in the job's `script.sh`. We read them and compare them with the
defaults of the installed `miic`:

```{r}
#| label: settings

script <- readLines(file.path(job_dir, "script.sh"), warn = FALSE)
tokens <- str_split(paste(script[str_detect(script, "run_whole_causalCCC")], collapse = " "), "\\s+")[[1]]

server_value <- function(option) {
  i <- match(option, tokens)
  if (is.na(i)) return(NA_character_)
  if (is.na(tokens[i + 1]) || str_starts(tokens[i + 1], "--")) "TRUE" else tokens[i + 1]
}
same_value <- function(a, b) {
  clean <- \(v) case_when(v %in% c("no", "FALSE") ~ "FALSE", v %in% c("yes", "TRUE") ~ "TRUE", TRUE ~ v)
  a <- clean(a); b <- clean(b)
  na <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(a)); nb <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(b))
  if_else(!is.na(na) & !is.na(nb), na == nb, a == b)
}

tribble(~server_option,         ~miic_argument,
        "--complexity",         "cplx",
        "--orientation",        "orientation",
        "--latent_variables",   "latent",
        "--test_MAR",           "test_mar",
        "--consistency",        "consistent",
        "--eff_n",              "n_eff",
        "--negative_info",      "negative_info",
        "--consensus_threshold", "consensus_threshold",
        "--max_iteration",      "max_iteration",
        "--n_threads",          "n_threads",
        "--orient_probab_ratio", "ori_proba_ratio",
        "--conf_shuffle",       "n_shuffles",
        "--conf_ratio",         "conf_threshold") |>
  mutate(server_value  = map_chr(server_option, server_value),
         miic_default  = map_chr(miic_argument, \(a) str_remove_all(paste(deparse(formals(miic)[[a]]), collapse = ""), '"')),
         differs       = !same_value(server_value, miic_default)) |>
  arrange(desc(differs))
```

The three settings that differ (`ori_proba_ratio`, `n_shuffles`, `conf_threshold`) change which links are kept and
how they are oriented. They are not mentioned in the paper.

## 7. No random seed is recorded

The confidence filter shuffles the data 100 times. The server script sets no seed:

```{r}
#| label: seed

any(str_detect(script, regex("seed", ignore_case = TRUE)))
```

With our own seed, the rerun of notebook 04 reproduces the decisions but not exactly the confidence ratios:

```{r}
#| label: confidence-ratios

rerun <- read_tsv(file.path(nb04_dir, "edges_rerun.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

inner_join(edges_authors |> transmute(link = link_name(x, y), confidence_authors = confidence),
           rerun |> transmute(link = link_name(x, y), confidence_ours = confidence),
           by = "link") |>
  summarise(shared_pairs_examined = n(),
            largest_difference = max(abs(confidence_authors - confidence_ours), na.rm = TRUE))
```

## 8. Our version of `miic` writes each L-R pair twice

The C++ reconstruction forces each L-R pair into the network (a *placeholder* row), and `summarizeResults()` then
appends the real row (maximum strength, ligand → receptor) without removing the placeholder:

```{r}
#| label: placeholders

res04 <- readRDS(file.path(nb04_dir, "miic_result.rds"))
raw   <- as_tibble(res04$all.edges.summary)
is_lr <- link_name(raw$x, raw$y) %in% lr_links

tibble(source = c("our run (miic, causalccc branch, commit 5ca0b22)", "authors' file"),
       rows_for_the_43_L_R_pairs = c(sum(is_lr), sum(link_name(edges_authors$x, edges_authors$y) %in% lr_links)),
       placeholders_computed_on_0_cells = c(sum(is_lr & raw$Nxy_ai %in% 0),
                                            sum(link_name(edges_authors$x, edges_authors$y) %in% lr_links &
                                                  edges_authors$Nxy_ai %in% 0)))
```

The server ran on 21 January 2025 and the branch commit we use is dated 23 January 2025, so the server cannot have run
this exact code. The version it used is not stated.

```{r}
#| label: miic-version

packageVersion("miic")
```

## 9. The computation is heavy

```{r}
#| label: run-times

tibble(step = c("MI tables for the gene selection (notebook 05)", "MIIC on the authors' input (notebook 04)"),
       time = c(format(round(attr(mi_tables, "run_time"), 1)), format(round(attr(res04, "run_time"), 1))))
```

The MIIC run lasts about 3 hours on one thread, and the server's own run is of the same order (see `whole_run.log`). A
run with 4 threads crashed in our hands (C stack errors, notebook 06), so the single-thread setting cannot be
sped up.

# Part 5 – Consequence on the network

## 10. The orientations depend on the duplicates

We compare the authors' network with the one obtained by running MIIC on their input **without** the duplicated
columns (saved in notebook 07, section 5):

```{r}
#| label: dedup-network

dedup_result <- readRDS(file.path(nb07_dir, "authors_dedup", "miic_result.rds"))
edges_dedup  <- as_tibble(dedup_result$all.edges.summary) |>
  filter(!(link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links & Nxy_ai %in% 0))   # placeholder rows (section 8)

# Every variable identified as "<gene>_<cell type>": the two copies of a duplicated gene become one node
key_of <- tibble(variable = names(mosaic), cell_type = col_type) |>
  mutate(key = if_else(str_detect(variable, "^(labels|condition)_"), variable,
                       paste0(strip(variable), "_", cell_type))) |>
  pull(key, name = variable)

gene_links <- function(edge_list) {
  edge_list |>
    filter(type == "P") |>
    mutate(a = key_of[x], b = key_of[y]) |>
    filter(a != b, !link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links) |>
    transmute(link = link_name(a, b),
              orientation = if_else(a == pmin(a, b) | infOrt %in% c(1, 6), infOrt, -infOrt),
              is_causal) |>
    distinct(link, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

net_authors <- gene_links(edges_authors)
net_dedup   <- gene_links(edges_dedup)
shared      <- inner_join(net_authors, net_dedup, by = "link", suffix = c("_authors", "_dedup"))

tibble(links_authors = nrow(net_authors),
       links_without_duplicates = nrow(net_dedup),
       jaccard_of_the_links = nrow(shared) / n_distinct(c(net_authors$link, net_dedup$link)),
       same_orientation = mean(shared$orientation_authors == shared$orientation_dedup),
       reversed = sum(abs(shared$orientation_authors) == 2 & shared$orientation_authors == -shared$orientation_dedup),
       genuine_causations_authors = sum(net_authors$is_causal == "Y"),
       genuine_causations_without_duplicates = sum(net_dedup$is_causal == "Y"),
       genuine_causations_in_both = sum(shared$is_causal_authors == "Y" & shared$is_causal_dedup == "Y")) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value")
```

The links do not change, but the orientation of a fraction of them does: MIIC's orientations are much more sensitive to
the input than its links. The orientation claims of the paper therefore depend on an artefact of the preparation.

# Part 6 – What we could not check

## 11. The preprocessing of the data is not described

No document describes how the Seurat object (cells, quality control, normalisation, annotation) was obtained from the
raw data of He *et al.* We tried to rebuild one of the eight samples from its FASTQ files
(`notebooks/case2/preprocessing/`). The cells are found again and their expression is correlated with CellChat's, but
the agreement is only partial: the preprocessing parameters of the CellChat dataset are not available, so the exact
counts cannot be recovered this way. The counts can be recovered exactly only from the CellChat matrix (section 1),
which does not tell us how it was produced.

## 12. The sources are fragile

```{r}
#| label: sources

list.files(job_dir)

tibble(file = "data_humanSkin_CellChat.rda",
       md5_of_our_copy = unname(tools::md5sum(cellchat)),
       md5_recorded_in_data_README = "9d31f4c88be64912b937b5d6a2cb6c2d") |>
  mutate(same = md5_of_our_copy == md5_recorded_in_data_README)
```

The CausalCCC server is not an archive: the authors' job files could disappear. The figshare link of the CellChat
dataset refused scripted downloads on 2026-10-05, so that file has to be downloaded by hand.

# Summary

| # | Limit | Evidence | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Raw counts not provided | CellChat values are not integers | counts can only be recovered by undoing the normalisation |
| 2 | Wrapper does not run as published | `slot` error with Seurat 5; data frame input; one sender and receiver; wrong suffixes | the authors' table did not come from a single call; their parameters are unknown |
| 3 | Selection settings undocumented | exact match only with 25 genes, no cap of 8, `labels` and `condition` | default settings recover only part of the authors' genes |
| 4 | Duplicated columns in the input | 14 identical column pairs in `input.tsv` | one gene counted as two variables; pooling script unavailable |
| 5 | Strongest link is an artefact | two copies of a gene linked at maximum strength | the strength of all L-R links comes from the duplicate |
| 6 | MIIC settings differ from `miic()` defaults | three settings differ (`ori_proba_ratio`, `n_shuffles`, `conf_threshold`) | must be copied from `script.sh`; not in the paper |
| 7 | No random seed | no seed in `script.sh` | confidence ratios differ slightly between runs |
| 8 | Version differences | 86 rows instead of 43 for the L-R pairs | placeholders must be removed; exact version unknown |
| 9 | Heavy computation | about 3 hours on one thread; multithreading crashed | hard to rerun and to test variants |
| 10 | Orientations depend on the duplicates | links unchanged, a fraction of orientations differ | causal claims depend on an artefact |
| 11 | Preprocessing not described | partial agreement when rebuilt from FASTQ | the Seurat object cannot be reproduced |
| 12 | Fragile sources | server not an archive; figshare refuses scripts | data may become unavailable |

**What we did not test.** Adding the duplicated columns to our rebuilt input and checking that MIIC returns the authors'
network exactly (notebook 07, "What we did not test"). This would confirm that the duplicates are the only remaining
difference.

## Session information

```{r}
#| label: session-info

sessionInfo()
```
